open_questions: Why the combined fit still gives a flat-bottomed shape with no secondary
dossier.public_summary: The dip alternates between a deep and a shallow transit, indicating an eclipsing binary folded at 12.9 days rather than a planet. Only three noisy transits are inconsistent in depth and the signal is ranked very low as planet-like.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits have very different depths (odd 2.7x deeper); change is confirmed per sector with 3.52 sigma, consistent with a binary folded at twice the true period rather than a planet.
reasons.value: diff_sigma=3.52, depth_odd_ppm=16210 vs depth_even_ppm=6034, depth_difference=0.6277, depth_ratio=2.7, sector_oe_max_sigma=4.391, sector_oe_sectors_over_3=1

reasons.why: Individual transit depths do not agree; low SNR (11.01) and only 3 transits produce a statistically significant scatter, supporting the odd/even difference is not noise.
Machine-learning rank is very low (median planet is 0.5; <0.1 is strongly planet-unlike), consistent with the odd/even and transit-scatter evidence for an eclipsing binary.
